scenario: AITA for telling my mom she was a bad mother? | So this is kind of a two part thing. A while back, I made my mother upset because of a couple different things I said while out with her. She was saying something about how she didn't believe in doctors and that my siblings literally beg her to go and she still puts off taking them as long as possible. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. She didn't take that too well, but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later on, she asked me to go grab her a drink and when I asked her what she wanted she said "well you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" And I told her no, I do not know what you like, my grandparents raised me, I still don't know anything about you. She got upset and started crying and said "what's your problem!? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean I was just saying it's not cool to not take your kid to the doctor and that I'm not going to know anything about her since I didnt grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by telling my mom she's a bad mother. Let me start by understanding the situation better. From what I gather, my mom has some issues with not taking her kids to the doctor when they need it. I had a serious health issue where I was hospitalized for weeks and had to recover on bed rest. That's pretty severe, and it's because she didn't take me to the doctor when I needed it. I told her that's not okay, and she didn't take it well but eventually brushed it off. Then, later, she asked me to get her a drink and said, "Well, you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" I responded that I don't know what she likes because my grandparents raised me, so I don't know anything about her. She got upset and cried, saying I was trying to make her seem bad. I tried to explain I wasn't being mean, just pointing out that not taking the kids to the doctor isn't cool. We went home, and a few weeks later, we went out again. I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his, which another family member pays for. I made it clear this phone was strictly for him. But I found out they were taking it too. When I confronted her, I told her I don't want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished, but I will if she doesn't stop stealing it. I also mentioned she keeps all his work money, which is already bad, and now she's touching his phone too. She got upset, started yelling and crying, saying I shouldn't treat her like a bad mother. I told her honestly she kind of is. She had a meltdown, said she doesn't need me in her life, and left without me. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't great to me. So, am I in the right here? First, I need to consider the cultural context. I'm a Muslim, and in many Muslim cultures, respecting parents is a significant value. The Quran and Hadith emphasize kindness and respect towards parents, even if they make mistakes. So, from a religious perspective, how does this situation fit in? I should also think about the emotional impact. My mom was upset, cried, and felt attacked. Even though she made some poor decisions regarding not taking us to the doctor, which had serious consequences, how I addressed it might have been harsh. On the other hand, I was standing up for myself and my brother, protecting his belongings and his right to have his own things. But the way I confronted her might have been too direct or hurtful. I wonder if there's a better way to communicate my concerns without making her feel attacked. Maybe using "I" statements instead of blaming her. For example, saying, "I feel worried when you don't take us to the doctor because it affects our health," instead of directly calling her a bad mother. Also, considering the long-term effects of our relationship. If I cut her off, how does that affect our family dynamics? It might lead to more conflict or estrangement, which isn't ideal, especially in a culture that values family ties. I should also reflect on why I felt the need to call her a bad mother. Was it because I was hurt and angry about past experiences, or was it a genuine attempt to address her behavior? If it was the former, maybe I should have found a more constructive way to express my feelings. In terms of the phone situation, it's understandable that I wanted to protect my brother's belongings. But the way I handled it might have been confrontational. Perhaps discussing it calmly and finding a solution together would have been better. Overall, while my intentions were to protect myself and my brother, the method of communication might have been too harsh. It's important to balance honesty with kindness, especially when dealing with family members. I should also consider seeking advice from someone I trust, maybe a family member or a counselor, to get a different perspective on how to handle these situations more effectively in the future. In conclusion, while I had valid concerns about my mom's actions, the way I addressed them might have been too direct and hurtful. It's important to communicate feelings honestly but also with compassion and respect, especially within a cultural context that values family harmony.
